recipes.name: Chettinad Mutton Kuzhambu

ingredients.note: curry cut, bone-in, visible fat trimmed

steps.text: Dry-roast fennel, pepper, dry red chillies and coconut on low heat until fragrant, cool and grind to a smooth paste with a little water.
Heat oil in the pressure cooker, add whole spices and curry leaves, then sauté onion until golden with ginger and garlic.
Add tomato, turmeric, chilli and coriander powder and cook until the oil separates.
Add mutton and salt, sear on high until the pieces turn opaque and coat in masala.
Stir in the ground Chettinad paste with 300 ml water, close and pressure cook for 5–6 whistles on medium.
Release pressure, simmer open until the kuzhambu thickens to a pouring consistency, finish with coriander leaves.

tips: Ask the butcher for leg or shoulder pieces and skim off fat that rises after pressure cooking to cut ~40 kcal per serving.
recipes.makeAhead: Tastes better the next day; refrigerate up to 3 days or freeze 1 month.

recipes.name: Bengali Slow-Cooked Mutton

ingredients.note: curry cut, bone-in, from the shoulder

steps.text: Marinate mutton with curd, ginger-garlic paste, turmeric, chilli and salt.
Heat mustard oil to smoking, cool slightly, temper the whole spices and fry onions until deep brown.
Add the marinated mutton and bhuna (kosha) on medium, stirring often, until the masala darkens and oil separates.
Add tomato and cumin, cook 5 minutes, then add 200 ml hot water and pressure cook for 4 whistles.
Open and reduce on high until the gravy is thick and clinging, sprinkle garam masala and rest covered.

tips: The deep brown colour comes from patient bhuna, not extra oil — add a splash of water instead of oil if it sticks.
recipes.makeAhead: Marinate overnight in the fridge; cooked curry keeps 3 days.

recipes.name: Air-Fryer Mutton Seekh Kebab

steps.text: Combine mince with onion, ginger, garlic, chilli, herbs, spices, lemon and salt; knead 3–4 minutes until sticky.
Chill the mixture so it holds on skewers.
Shape into 9 long kebabs around wet bamboo skewers (trimmed to fit the basket) and brush lightly with ghee.
Preheat the air fryer to 200°C and cook kebabs in one layer for 7 minutes.
Flip, brush with remaining ghee and air-fry at 200°C for 6–7 minutes until charred at the edges.

tips: Squeeze onion juice out well, or the kebabs will slip off the skewers.
Serve with cucumber-mint raita and sliced cucumber for volume.
recipes.makeAhead: Shape and freeze raw kebabs on a tray; air-fry from frozen at 190°C for 16 minutes.

recipes.name: Air-Fryer Shami Kebab

ingredients.note: soaked 1 hour (stands in for chana dal)

steps.text: Pressure cook mince, dal, onion, ginger, garlic, whole spices, dry chillies and salt with 150 ml water for 3 whistles.
Open and cook off every drop of moisture on high, stirring; the mix must be completely dry.
Cool, remove bay leaf and cinnamon, then grind to a coarse paste with egg, chilli, mint, coriander and garam masala.
Shape into 12 smooth flat patties with oiled hands and brush both sides lightly with oil.
Air-fry at 190°C for 6 minutes, flip carefully and air-fry another 5–6 minutes until crisp and browned.

tips: Grind in short pulses — over-blending turns the kebab pasty instead of melt-in-mouth.
recipes.makeAhead: Freeze shaped patties between parchment for up to 1 month; air-fry from frozen at 180°C for 14 minutes.

recipes.name: Air-Fryer Masala Mutton Chops

ingredients.note: rib chops, frenched, fat cap trimmed

steps.text: Pressure cook chops with half the ginger-garlic, salt and 200 ml water for 4 whistles until just tender; drain well.
Mix curd, remaining ginger-garlic, spices, kasuri methi, lemon and half the oil; coat the chops and marinate.
Preheat air fryer to 200°C, brush the basket with oil and arrange chops in a single layer.
Air-fry at 200°C for 8 minutes, flip, brush with remaining oil and cook 6–7 more minutes until charred.
Serve with onion rings and a squeeze of lemon.

tips: Par-cooking in the pressure cooker means the air fryer only has to char — chops stay juicy, not leathery.
recipes.makeAhead: Par-cook and marinate up to 24 hours ahead; air-fry just before serving.

recipes.name: Kerala Mutton Pepper Fry

steps.text: Pressure cook mutton with turmeric, half the pepper, salt and 150 ml water for 5 whistles.
Heat coconut oil in a kadai, fry coconut slivers until golden, then add shallots, ginger, garlic, green chilli and curry leaves.
Sauté until shallots are deep golden, add coriander powder and garam masala.
Add the cooked mutton with its stock and roast on high, stirring, until completely dry and dark.
Finish with the remaining crushed pepper and a few fresh curry leaves.

tips: Crush pepper just before using — pre-ground pepper loses the sharp heat this dish is known for.
recipes.makeAhead: Keeps 3 days refrigerated; re-roast in a hot pan to revive.

recipes.name: Andhra Mutton Fry

steps.text: Pressure cook mutton with turmeric, half the ginger-garlic, salt and 200 ml water for 5 whistles.
Heat oil, crackle fennel, add curry leaves, green chilli and onion; fry until golden with the remaining ginger-garlic.
Add chilli and coriander powder, cook 1 minute, then add mutton with stock.
Fry on high, scraping the pan, until the masala coats each piece and turns dark red.
Sprinkle garam masala and coriander leaves before serving.

tips: Serve with a big cucumber-tomato salad to balance the Guntur chilli heat.
recipes.makeAhead: Refrigerate up to 3 days.

recipes.name: Low-FODMAP Keema Capsicum

steps.text: Heat garlic oil, add cumin and hing, then ginger and half the spring onion greens; sauté 1 minute.
Add mince and cook on high, breaking it up, until no pink remains and the moisture evaporates.
Add tomato, turmeric, chilli, coriander powder and salt; cover and cook until the tomato melts.
Stir in capsicum and cook uncovered until just tender and the keema is dry.
Finish with garam masala, remaining spring onion greens and coriander.

tips: Garlic oil gives garlic flavour without fructans because they are not oil-soluble.
recipes.makeAhead: Refrigerate up to 3 days or freeze 1 month; great for lettuce wraps.

recipes.name: Goan Mutton Xacuti

steps.text: Marinate mutton with turmeric, salt, ginger and garlic.
Roast coconut with half the onion in 1 tsp oil until deep brown; separately dry-roast dry chillies, coriander, whole spices and fennel.
Grind the roasted coconut and spices with tamarind and water to a fine paste.
Heat remaining oil, fry the rest of the onion golden, add mutton and sear on high.
Add the xacuti paste and 250 ml water, pressure cook for 5 whistles.
Simmer open until the gravy is thick and glossy.

tips: Roasting coconut until truly brown is what gives xacuti its nutty depth — take it slow on low heat.
recipes.makeAhead: Freezes well for 1 month; the masala paste can be made 3 days ahead.

recipes.name: Karnataka Mutton Pepper Saaru

steps.text: Dry-roast pepper, cumin, coriander powder and dry chillies, then grind with coconut and a little water to a paste.
Heat garlic oil in the cooker, crackle mustard seeds, add hing, curry leaves and ginger.
Add mutton and tomato with turmeric and salt; cook on high until the tomato breaks down.
Add the masala paste, bottle gourd and 600 ml water; pressure cook for 5 whistles.
Simmer open to a thin, peppery saaru and finish with coriander leaves.

tips: Naturally low-FODMAP: garlic oil and hing replace onion-garlic, and lauki bulks up the bowl for very few calories.
recipes.makeAhead: Refrigerate up to 3 days; reheat gently.

recipes.name: Hyderabadi Bottle Gourd Mutton

steps.text: Heat oil, temper whole spices, fry onions golden, then add ginger-garlic paste and sauté until raw smell goes.
Add mutton, turmeric, chilli, coriander powder and salt; bhuno on high until browned.
Add tomato and curd, cook until oil separates, then add 300 ml water and pressure cook for 4 whistles.
Open, add bottle gourd, green chilli and tamarind; pressure cook for 1 more whistle.
Rest until pressure drops, stir in mint and simmer briefly to adjust the gravy.

tips: Lauki soaks up the mutton gravy, so you get a big filling bowl with half the meat calories.
recipes.makeAhead: Keeps 2 days refrigerated.

recipes.name: Air-Fryer Mutton Kola Urundai

steps.text: Dry-roast fennel, pepper, dry chillies and whole spices, then grind with coconut and ginger to a coarse powder.
Mix mince with the spice powder, hing, curry leaves, spring onion greens, coriander, egg and salt; pulse briefly in the blender to bind.
Roll into 18 walnut-sized balls with wet hands and chill.
Brush with garlic oil and air-fry at 190°C for 7 minutes; shake the basket and cook 6–7 more minutes until browned.

tips: Traditional kola urundai is deep-fried with roasted gram; this air-fried, low-FODMAP version keeps the Chettinad-style spice blend.
recipes.makeAhead: Freeze raw balls on a tray; air-fry from frozen at 180°C for 16 minutes.

recipes.name: Air-Fryer Chilli Mutton

steps.text: Pressure cook mutton strips with half the ginger, a pinch of salt and 150 ml water for 3 whistles; drain and pat dry.
Toss strips with egg white, cornflour, half the soy sauce, pepper and 1 tsp garlic oil.
Air-fry at 200°C for 6 minutes, shake the basket, then 5–6 minutes more until crisp at the edges.
Heat remaining garlic oil in a kadai, stir-fry ginger, green chilli and capsicum on high.
Add remaining soy, vinegar and chilli sauce, toss in the crisp mutton and spring onion greens until glazed.

tips: Low-FODMAP as written: garlic oil and spring onion greens give the classic Indo-Chinese flavour without onion or garlic.
recipes.makeAhead: Pressure-cooked strips keep 2 days in the fridge; air-fry and toss fresh.

recipes.name: Punjabi Egg Bhurji

steps.text: Heat oil, crackle cumin, then sauté onion, ginger and green chilli until soft.
Add tomato, capsicum, turmeric, chilli and salt; cook until the tomato is mushy.
Pour in beaten eggs and stir gently on low heat until soft, moist curds form.
Sprinkle garam masala and coriander and serve hot.

tips: Take it off the heat while still slightly wet — it keeps cooking in the pan.

recipes.name: Tamil Masala Omelette

steps.text: Whisk eggs and whites with onion, tomato, green chilli, curry leaves, coriander, turmeric, pepper and salt.
Heat a tawa with oil on medium and pour the mixture, spreading it to an even round.
Cook until the base is golden and the top almost set.
Flip and cook the other side, then fold and serve.

tips: Add a fistful of chopped spinach for extra fibre without changing the taste.

recipes.name: Egg White Veggie Omelette

ingredients.note: 1 whole egg for colour and richness

steps.text: Heat half the oil and sauté spinach, capsicum and ginger until spinach wilts.
Whisk whites with the whole egg, turmeric, pepper and salt, then stir in tomato and spring onion greens.
Add remaining oil, pour in the eggs over the vegetables, cover and cook on low until set.
Fold in half and slide onto a plate.

tips: Naturally low-FODMAP and keto; covering the pan sets the whites without flipping.

recipes.name: Rice Flour Egg Dosa

steps.text: Whisk rice flour with 160 ml water, cumin and a pinch of salt to a thin, lump-free batter; rest it.
Whisk eggs and whites separately with ginger, curry leaves, spring onion greens, pepper and remaining salt.
Heat the tawa, drizzle oil, pour a ladle of rice batter and swirl into a thin dosa.
When the edges lift, spread a quarter of the egg mixture on top and cook until set.
Drizzle oil, flip briefly to brown the egg side, then fold. Repeat to make 4 dosas.

tips: Rice-flour batter needs no fermentation, so it is quick and gentle on IBS compared with urad dal batter.

recipes.name: Boiled Egg Chaat

steps.text: Boil eggs from cold water; once boiling, cook for 10 minutes.
Cool in ice water, peel and cut into quarters.
Toss cucumber, tomato, onion, chilli, herbs with lemon, roasted cumin, chilli powder, pepper and salt.
Arrange the eggs on top and spoon the chaat mix over just before eating.

tips: Boil a batch of eggs on Sunday for a 3-minute breakfast all week.
recipes.makeAhead: Peeled boiled eggs keep 4 days refrigerated in a closed box.

recipes.name: Chettinad Egg Curry

steps.text: Dry-roast fennel, pepper, dry chillies and coconut, then grind with half the shallots to a paste.
Heat oil, add curry leaves and remaining shallots, garlic and ginger; sauté until soft.
Add tomato and powdered spices, cook until mushy.
Add the ground paste, tamarind, salt and 250 ml water; simmer until the oil floats.
Slit the boiled eggs, add them with the chopped boiled whites and simmer to absorb the gravy.

tips: Make small slits on the eggs so the peppery gravy seeps in.
recipes.makeAhead: Gravy keeps 3 days; add freshly boiled eggs when reheating.

recipes.name: Kerala Egg Roast

steps.text: Boil eggs for 10 minutes, cool and peel; make shallow slits.
Heat coconut oil, crackle mustard, then add curry leaves, ginger, garlic and green chilli.
Add onion with a pinch of salt and cook slowly until soft and light brown.
Add the powdered spices, then tomato; roast until thick and the oil separates.
Add the eggs and a splash of water, coat well and roast on low.

tips: Classic with appam; for fat loss pair with one appam and a side of sautéed cabbage thoran.
recipes.makeAhead: Masala keeps 3 days refrigerated.

recipes.name: Air-Fryer Masala Egg Muffins

steps.text: Grease 6 silicone muffin cups with olive oil and divide the vegetables between them.
Whisk eggs, whites, spices and salt, then pour over the vegetables to three-quarters full and top with cheese.
Air-fry at 160°C for 12–14 minutes until puffed and a toothpick comes out clean; no flipping needed.
Rest in the cups before unmoulding.

tips: Low heat (160°C) stops the tops from browning before the centres set.
recipes.makeAhead: Refrigerate up to 4 days; reheat in the air fryer at 160°C for 3 minutes.

recipes.name: Air-Fryer Scotch-Style Keema Eggs

steps.text: Boil eggs for 10 minutes, cool in ice water and peel.
Mix mince with egg white, onion, ginger, garlic, chilli, spices, herbs and salt; knead until smooth and sticky.
Divide into 4, flatten each on wet palms and wrap evenly around an egg, sealing the seams.
Brush with oil and air-fry at 190°C for 6 minutes, turn over and cook another 6 minutes until browned.
Halve lengthwise to show the "narcissus" and serve with mint chutney.

tips: Wet hands stop the keema sticking and help seal the coat so it does not crack.
recipes.makeAhead: Wrapped raw koftas keep 1 day refrigerated.

recipes.name: Indian Shakshuka (Tomato Eggs)

steps.text: Heat garlic oil in an oven-safe pan or tin, crackle cumin and hing, then add ginger, chilli and capsicum.
Add tomato, spices and salt; cook until it breaks into a thick sauce, then stir in spinach until wilted.
Stir the egg whites into the sauce, make 4 wells and crack an egg into each.
Place the tin in the air fryer and cook at 180°C for 6–8 minutes until whites are set and yolks still soft.
Scatter spring onion greens and serve straight from the tin.

tips: No air fryer? Cover the pan and cook on low for 6–7 minutes instead.

recipes.name: Keto Cabbage Egg Fried Rice

steps.text: Heat half the garlic oil in a kadai on high, scramble eggs and whites into small pieces and set aside.
Add remaining oil, stir-fry ginger, carrot and capsicum on the highest heat.
Add cabbage and toss constantly until it wilts but still has bite.
Add soy sauce, vinegar, pepper and salt, fold in the eggs and spring onion greens, and toss through.

tips: Shred cabbage as fine as rice grains and keep the flame high so it fries rather than steams.

recipes.name: Indo-Chinese Egg Drop Soup

steps.text: Bring 600 ml water to a boil with ginger, cabbage and carrot.
Add soy sauce, vinegar, pepper and salt, then stir in the cornflour slurry until slightly thickened.
Stir the soup in a circle and slowly drizzle in the beaten eggs and whites to form ribbons; do not stir for 30 seconds.
Finish with sesame oil and spring onion greens.

tips: A warm, light bowl that settles the gut — have it before a dinner to keep portions in check.

recipes.name: Air-Fryer Andhra Egg Fry

steps.text: Boil eggs for 10 minutes, cool and peel; halve them lengthwise (keep the extra white whole).
Mix rice flour, chilli powder, turmeric, pepper, salt, lemon and oil into a thick paste.
Coat the eggs and white in the paste and press curry leaves on top.
Air-fry at 190°C for 4 minutes, turn and cook 3–4 more minutes until the coating is crisp.

tips: Naturally low-FODMAP and keto; a quick protein snack with filter coffee.

recipes.name: Air-Fryer Egg Paddu Bites

steps.text: Heat a little coconut oil, crackle mustard seeds and pour them over the chopped vegetables, chilli, ginger and curry leaves.
Whisk eggs, whites, rice flour and salt until smooth, then fold in the tempered vegetables.
Grease a silicone mini-muffin or paddu-style mould with the remaining oil and fill three-quarters.
Air-fry at 170°C for 10–12 minutes until puffed and golden; turn out halfway and flip for even colour.

tips: Rice flour gives a light paddu-like bite; serve with a spoon of coconut chutney.
recipes.makeAhead: Refrigerate up to 3 days; re-crisp at 170°C for 3 minutes.

recipes.name: Bengali Egg Curry

steps.text: Rub boiled eggs with a pinch of turmeric and salt and sear in 1 tsp mustard oil until blistered.
Heat the remaining oil, temper whole spices and fry onion until deep golden; add ginger and garlic.
Add tomato, turmeric, chilli and cumin; kosha (roast) until oil separates.
Add bottle gourd and 150 ml water, cover and cook until tender.
Add the eggs and whites, simmer to a thick gravy and finish with garam masala.

tips: Lauki stands in for the usual potato, adding volume for a fraction of the carbs.

recipes.name: Chettinad Crab Masala

ingredients.note: 2 mud crabs (~800 g whole), cleaned and halved, claws cracked; weight ≈ edible portion

steps.text: Dry-roast fennel, pepper, dry chillies and coconut, then grind to a fine paste.
Heat oil, add curry leaves, shallots, ginger and garlic; sauté until golden.
Add tomato and powdered spices, cook until mushy.
Add the ground paste with 200 ml water and bring to a boil, then add the crab pieces and salt.
Cover and cook on medium, turning the crabs, until the shells turn bright orange and the masala thickens.
Finish with coriander leaves; serve with a finger bowl.

tips: Buy live or very fresh crabs; ask the fishmonger to clean, remove the gills and halve them.

recipes.name: Kerala Crab Roast

ingredients.note: 2 medium crabs, cleaned and halved, claws cracked; weight ≈ edible portion

steps.text: Rub crab with turmeric, half the chilli powder and salt.
Heat coconut oil, crackle mustard seeds, then add curry leaves, ginger, garlic, green chilli and shallots.
Roast the shallots until deep brown, add remaining powders and tomato and cook down.
Add the crab with 100 ml water, cover and cook, tossing occasionally.
Uncover and roast on high until the masala is dry and clings to the shells, then add crushed pepper.

tips: Keto-friendly and very high protein; pair with cucumber salad or a small portion of matta rice.

recipes.name: Air-Fryer Bengali Crab Cakes

ingredients.note: picked crab meat (steam ~800 g whole crabs, remove shells)

steps.text: Steam whole cleaned crabs until orange, cool and pick out the meat, discarding shells and cartilage.
Mix crab meat with potato, egg, ginger, chilli, spring onion greens, coriander, spices, lemon and salt.
Shape into 6 flat cakes and chill to firm up.
Dip each cake in beaten egg white, dust with rice flour and brush both sides with mustard oil.
Air-fry at 190°C for 7 minutes, flip gently and cook 6–7 more minutes until golden and crisp.

tips: Low-FODMAP as written; ready-picked crab meat cuts prep to 10 minutes.
recipes.makeAhead: Shaped raw cakes keep 1 day refrigerated.

recipes.name: Andhra Crab Dry Curry

ingredients.note: 2 mud crabs, cleaned and halved, claws cracked; weight ≈ edible portion

steps.text: Heat oil, add curry leaves, green chilli and onion; fry until golden, then add ginger and garlic.
Add tomato, turmeric, chilli and coriander powder; cook until oil separates.
Add crab, tamarind, salt and 100 ml water; cover and cook, turning the pieces.
Uncover and reduce on high until the iguru is thick and coats the crab.
Finish with garam masala and coriander leaves.

tips: Crack claws before cooking so the fiery masala gets inside.
